title: Knowledge check: Using the Flask Test Client

questions.prompt: Which source-syllabus topic is explicitly covered by “Using the Flask Test Client”?
options: Flask's purpose in Python web development
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “GET and POST requests” under lesson 174, “Using the Flask Test Client”. Keep this subtopic aligned to its module and confirm version-sensitive details in the official Flask documentation.

questions.prompt: When applying “Using the Flask Test Client” in a real Flask application, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Trust the browser and skip server-side checks.
Change several parts at once and infer success from one happy-path request.
Use a small reproducible example and test both expected behavior and a meaningful failure boundary.
Expose internal tracebacks to the caller to simplify debugging.
questions.answer_key: Use a small reproducible example and test both expected behavior and a meaningful failure boundary.
questions.explanation: For using the flask test client, use the matching official documentation, a narrow example, and a test of both normal and invalid conditions. Browser validation alone and exposed tracebacks are not reliable safeguards.

questions.prompt: Which design principle best complements “Using the Flask Test Client” as the course moves toward production?
options: Separate Flask core behavior from optional extension or infrastructure behavior, validate untrusted input at the server boundary, and document the runtime assumptions.
Assume a green diagram proves correctness without running a test.
Assume Flask automatically provides a database, authentication system and task queue.
Treat a development server or debug mode as the production deployment plan.
questions.answer_key: Separate Flask core behavior from optional extension or infrastructure behavior, validate untrusted input at the server boundary, and document the runtime assumptions.
questions.explanation: Flask is a lightweight framework whose databases, account management, caching and task queues commonly come from separately selected tools. Verify trust boundaries and runtime assumptions with tests.
